notice: RN bank batch 123: Hematologic and oncologic case studies: pernicious anemia, spinal cord compression, extravasation and TTP, with four standalone items. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: After reading the note, complete the diagram with the condition the client is most likely experiencing, the 2 actions the nurse should take first, and the 2 parameters to monitor.

actions.text: Give calcium gluconate IV as prescribed
Give regular insulin with dextrose IV as prescribed
Give sodium polystyrene as the only treatment
Encourage the client to drink orange juice
Start lactated Ringer's at a fast rate

rationale.correct: Peaked T waves and a wide QRS with potassium 7.2 need calcium and an insulin shift now.

perOption.c1: Potassium 7.2 with peaked T waves and a wide QRS.
perOption.c2: Would not explain the ECG pattern this strongly.
perOption.a1: Stabilizes the heart membrane in minutes.
perOption.a3: Too slow alone for these ECG changes.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize and act on severe hyperkalemia.

exhibits.title: Renal unit
exhibits.body: A client with kidney failure missed dialysis for 4 days. Potassium 7.2 mEq/L. ECG: peaked T waves and a widened QRS. Heart rate 52/min. Glucose 104 mg/dL.

questions.stem: A client receiving chemotherapy has blood counts each week. For each trend, choose the interpretation.

options.text: Nadir around day 10; neutropenic precautions now
A slow fall; monitor for fatigue

rationale.correct: Neutrophils and platelets reach their nadir around days 7 to 14; precautions match the counts.

perOption.b1:a: The lowest point is when infection risk peaks.
perOption.b2:c: Usually only below 10,000 or with bleeding.
perOption.b3:a: Red cells live longer, so they fall slowly.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Laboratory reference ranges as used in common NCLEX review texts; follow the facility's ranges
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: On an oncology unit at the start of the shift, four clients have needs. Whose bedside should the nurse go to first?

options.text: A client with leukemia whose platelet count is 18,000/mm3 and who has a few petechiae on the shins
A client with lung cancer who reports new back pain and leg heaviness since the night
A client with lymphoma whose antiemetic is due before the 0900 chemotherapy
A client with colon cancer who asks to talk about stopping treatment and going home

rationale.correct: New back pain with leg symptoms in a client with cancer is cord compression until proven otherwise.

perOption.a: Expected with this count; maintain bleeding precautions.
perOption.b: Possible spinal cord compression; delay causes permanent paralysis.
perOption.d: Important; arrange time after the urgent client.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: Which tasks can the RN delegate to the UAP on a renal unit? Select all that apply.

options.text: Weighing clients on the same scale before breakfast
Reporting a client's report of a missing fistula thrill
Teaching a client on fluid restriction how to spread the allowance across the day
Removing the peritoneal dialysis effluent bag and judging whether it is cloudy

rationale.correct: UAPs weigh clients and measure output; assessment and teaching stay with the RN.

perOption.c: Assessing the thrill is the RN's role.

questions.stem: Complete the sentences by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The most likely cause is {{b1}}, made worse by {{b2}}. Giving folic acid alone would be dangerous because it {{b3}}.

options.text: metformin and omeprazole, which reduce B12 absorption
corrects the anemia while the nerve damage keeps progressing

questions.stem: For each order, indicate whether it is appropriate or not appropriate.

rows.text: Cyanocobalamin 1,000 mcg IM daily for a week, then weekly, then monthly
Potassium level in the first days of treatment
Fall prevention with a night light
Oral B12 at a standard daily dose as the only treatment

rationale.correct: IM B12 for life, potassium monitoring and fall prevention.

perOption.r2:c1: Pernicious anemia does not go away.
perOption.r2:c2: Pernicious anemia does not go away.
perOption.r3:c1: New red cell production can lower potassium.
perOption.r3:c2: New red cell production can lower potassium.
perOption.r5:c1: Poor position sense in the dark.
perOption.r5:c2: Poor position sense in the dark.
perOption.r6:c1: Absorption is poor without intrinsic factor.
perOption.r6:c2: Absorption is poor without intrinsic factor.

questions.stem: On day 3 of B12 injections, the client reports muscle weakness and palpitations. Review the findings. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Place the client on a cardiac monitor as prescribed
Stop the B12 permanently because of the reaction
Give an extra B12 injection to speed up recovery of the nerves

rationale.correct: Red cell production uses potassium; replace it and monitor.

perOption.a: Hypokalemia from rapid red cell production.
perOption.d: This is an expected effect of recovery, not an allergy.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: At 3 months, for each statement or finding, indicate whether it shows improvement or understanding, or needs follow-up.

rows.text: "I'll stop the shots once my blood is normal."
"Some numbness is still there, but my balance is better."
"I'll keep up the gastroscopy my doctor suggested."

rationale.correct: Blood counts and symptoms improved; B12 is lifelong.

perOption.r4:c1: Nerve recovery is slow and may be incomplete.
perOption.r4:c2: Nerve recovery is slow and may be incomplete.
perOption.r5:c1: Pernicious anemia raises gastric cancer risk.
perOption.r5:c2: Pernicious anemia raises gastric cancer risk.

questions.stem: For each action, indicate its priority.

rows.text: Arrange a whole-spine MRI within 24 hours, ideally sooner
Insert a urinary catheter for the retention
Ask the client to walk to the bathroom to test strength
Plan radiation or surgery after the MRI

rationale.correct: Steroids and MRI first, then bladder care and definitive treatment.

perOption.r4:c1: Unstable spine; keep flat until assessed.
perOption.r4:c2: Unstable spine; keep flat until assessed.
perOption.r4:c3: Unstable spine; keep flat until assessed.

questions.stem: Which interventions should the nurse include until the spine is shown to be stable? Select all that apply.

options.text: Flat bed rest with log rolling
Neurologic checks of leg strength and sensation every 4 hours
Raise the head of the bed to 60 degrees for comfort
Let the client sit on the edge of the bed to eat meals

rationale.correct: Spinal precautions, neurologic checks and VTE prophylaxis.

perOption.e: Unsafe until the spine is cleared.

options.text: Give a proton pump inhibitor as prescribed
Give the dose in the morning
Stop the dexamethasone suddenly after radiation
Expect the steroid to reverse any weakness in a day without radiation

perOption.f: Radiation or surgery is still needed.

caseStudies.title: Pernicious anemia compared with iron deficiency

exhibits.title: Primary care
exhibits.body: A 68-year-old client reports 4 months of tiredness, a sore tongue, and numbness and tingling in both feet. The client has stumbled twice in the dark and has been more forgetful. The client takes metformin and omeprazole and has autoimmune hypothyroidism.

exhibits.title: Phone call and arrival
exhibits.body: A 63-year-old client with prostate cancer that has spread to the bones calls about 2 weeks of worsening mid-back pain that is worse lying down and at night. Today both legs feel heavy and the client has not passed urine since the morning.

rows.label: Back pain
cells: 8/10 at the T8 level, worse lying flat and with coughing

caseStudies.title: Vesicant chemotherapy extravasation and hazardous-drug safety

exhibits.title: Chemotherapy chair
exhibits.body: A 47-year-old client with breast cancer is receiving doxorubicin by IV push through a peripheral IV in the left forearm because the port is blocked. Halfway through, the client says the site burns.

exhibits.title: Emergency department
exhibits.body: A 32-year-old client comes in with tiredness, bruises on the legs and a headache. The partner says the client has been confused since the morning and had a brief episode of slurred speech.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
